[b]For those who ask for more accuracy and and realism, here is a redone version for a more accurate terms and situations.
[/b]
Sikirsk has recently found remnants of the crash, today this part was lifted out by the Sikirskian Company "Sibir - Civil-Naval Corporation". They pulled out of the water: The cockpit. This included logs from the Pilot and the First Officer, and a Black Box T-T consisting of vocal logs from the pilots. Oceanice claimed to help, but has now been banned from Sikirskian territory in all ways, mostly because of classified reasons.

Besides the logs, small parts of the engines have been discovered. With one of latest found parts having confirmed human interaction. Besides the engine being 60% being completly obliterated, Engineers still have confirmed that someone had broken several parts, which would lead to the engine most likely overheating and catching fire mid-flight, which aligns with the logs and the restructured and visualised scene.

The logs show that the First Officer went to the back of the airplane for a bathroom break, during this, the rear-mounted left engine burst into flames and the pilot tried to struggle the airplane into stability, this succeeded until automatic fire suppression systems failed, and the fire began to spread to the rest of the tail. The airplane was already in descent at this moment, heading towards northern Hydronia. Due to the flight's distance from land, the pilot reported to air traffic control that he would attempt to glide to the surface and make a water landing. The aircraft successfully descended to 10 thousand feet when the left engine firewall failed, allowing the fire to spread to the controls of the elevator, burning through and disabling the elevator, causing the aircraft to enter an uncontrolled decent.

Sikirskan Aviation Authorities have determined from readings from the black box that the elevator was stuck in the up position, causing the aircraft to nose up, stall, and then enter a flat spin. This spin resulted in the tail of the aircraft hitting the water before the rest of the plane, which the stress on the airframe broke the aircraft in two. The frontal part would come to rest on a large underwater peak, making it one of the first descovered pieces of the aircraft.

[b]Sikirsk Expansion, Week Three, further into the northern lands.[/b]
[sub]by Sikirsk[/sub]]

[b]Field Report: Week Three of Colonial Expansion in Velkarin Sector
[/b]
Date: 5th of June
Issued by: Bureau of Northern Settlements and Expansion Ministry

Three weeks into Phase I of the Sikirskian Southern Colonial Program, developments within the Velkarin Sector continue at a steady and disciplined pace. While the initial landing and outpost establishment have already been catalogued in earlier reports, this update provides a more grounded look at progress in the field as construction teams, patrol units, and civilian pioneers settle into early operational routines.

The area immediately surrounding Velkarin Base has undergone visible transformation. Prefabricated wall segments, reinforced with gravel-filled gabion baskets, now ring the central settlement core. These barriers, while temporary in design, offer protection against both sandstorms and potential wildlife incursions. By next week, planners expect to integrate active sensor modules along the southern perimeter wall, allowing for continuous movement tracking and terrain feedback.

Internal roads have begun to take shape. Using locally sourced crushed stone mixed with polymer binding agents from mainland depots, engineering crews have finalized the primary transit corridornamed Main Strip Alphawhich links the military staging yards on the east with the civilian living zones to the west. Roadside lighting units powered by foldable solar panels were installed yesterday. Early reports suggest they are holding up well against the frequent gusts and airborne grit.

In the civilian zones, foundation slabs for the first public infrastructure facilities are now being laid. These include the community ration depot, medical triage post, and basic multi-purpose assembly shelter. As of this writing, six of the promised thirty-two concrete civilian housing blocks are structurally complete, with another four nearing roof installation. Each block is capable of housing up to four families in segmented units with shaded walkways, ceiling vents, and integrated water points.

The surrounding terrain has also received increased attention. Survey drones operating in the 15 km buffer zone report signs of minor fauna movementprimarily dust lizards, small antelope-like creatures, and migratory birds nesting near dry creek beds. No signs of organized human presence have been seen beyond the previously recorded wanderers. However, all patrol units have been instructed to maintain passive-contact protocols should encounters recur. So far, no follow-up sightings have occurred.

Communications infrastructure is progressing, albeit slower than projected. Two of the planned four transmission masts are up and running, allowing semi-stable contact with Kharins Reach coastal landing zones and Central Command in northern Sikirsk. Occasional atmospheric interference has been reported during midday heatwves, but signal strength typically improves by evening. Civilian communications remain limited to official dispatch terminals located in administrative structures.

We have expanded further into the northern lands, we plan to connect our central-northern territory with our Western-northern mainland territory. This is a large amount of land which shall be treated fairly, and shall Sikirsk-inized. Luckily we now find more oceanic climates, more like our islands.

[i][b]End of Report. Glory to Sikirsk.
[/b][/i][/spoiler]
